plates.caption: of what a weather radar saw above it that week: it starts in the air the radar sampled, within 50 km of it, and runs on at the heading and ground speed the radar measured, carried for 8 hours — an assumption, so a stroke reads as a flight. More strokes, more of it. Not one night and not one kind of animal: the radar cannot tell birds from bats from insects.
plates.credit: Map: Natural Earth — 1:10m land, coastline and rivers (Public domain).

plates.caption: by 170 foxes, drawn a day at a time from its daily median position, the red nib where it has got to in its own journey. All of them start together on day one: the published tracks carry no dates, so this is no one season. A few journeys run off the plate.
